title: MolEmb: Multimodal Large Language Models Can Be Strong Molecular Embedding Models
tldr: MolEmb is a lightweight framework that adapts multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to generate molecular embeddings by aligning them with textual descriptions in a shared space. The study finds that MLLMs, originally designed for image and text processing, can also serve as general molecular embedding models, but the effectiveness depends significantly on the quality and context of the training data, as demonstrated using the MolCAR diagnostic benchmark.

provenance.claim: MolEmb is a lightweight framework that adapts multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to generate molecular embeddings by aligning them with textual descriptions in a shared space.

evidence.text: We introduce \textbf{MolEmb}, a lightweight framework that adapts MLLMs by aligning molecular profiles with textual descriptions in a shared embedding space using a bidirectional contrastive objective.

provenance.claim: The study finds that MLLMs, originally designed for image and text processing, can also serve as general molecular embedding models, but the effectiveness depends significantly on the quality and context of the training data, as demonstrated using the MolCAR diagnostic benchmark.

evidence.text: We further introduce \textbf{MolCAR}, a diagnostic benchmark for context-aware retrieval, and find that context-aware molecular embedding is primarily a data property of the supervision.

title: A General-Purpose Molecular Foundation Model Transfers Across Diverse Olfactory Tasks
tldr: Uni-Mol2, fine-tuned on the GS-LF benchmark, demonstrates versatility in diverse olfactory tasks. The model, without further deep-learning training, performs well in cross-dataset odor descriptor prediction, odorous-versus-odorless classification, enantiomer evaluation, and odor mixture discriminability. These findings suggest a 'train-once, transfer-across-tasks' approach for machine olfaction, implying chemically pretrained molecular representations as a robust foundation for transferable olfactory prediction.

title: External Evaluation of Multi-Agent AI Systems in Drug Discovery: A PRISMA-Informed Scoping Review of the External-Evaluation Gap
tldr: This PRISMA-informed scoping review highlights a gap in external evaluations of multi-agent AI systems in drug discovery. Only two systems, TrialGPT and Biomni, have been independently evaluated, but they fall outside the strict multi-agent boundary. This suggests that independent evaluation primarily focuses on single-agent, modular, and general-purpose systems rather than complex multi-agent architectures.

title: Hit-Triage Pretrained Transformer (Hit-TPT), an Interaction-Agnostic Graph-Transformer for Post-docking Enrichment
tldr: The paper addresses the challenge of post-docking enrichment in drug discovery by introducing Hit-Triage Pretrained Transformer (Hit-TPT), an interaction-agnostic graph-transformer model. This physics-oriented architecture, demonstrated through experimental results, significantly reduces false positives in virtual screening, offering a practical and generalizable approach to enhance hit-finding efficiency by prioritizing compounds with genuine, target-specific activity. However, the evidence presented is abstract-level, and further studies may be required to quantify its performance improvement compared to existing methods.

title: Rescuable Stagnation: A Diagnostic for Benchmark Suitability in LLM-Guided Materials Optimization
tldr: This paper proposes a diagnostic criterion, 'rescuable stagnation', to evaluate the suitability of benchmarks for materials optimization using LLM-guided methods. The approach is demonstrated on a benchmark derived from Materials Project data, revealing no statistically significant improvement by LLM-guided rescue over heuristic injection. This criterion allows for testing benchmark suitability before experiments commence, ensuring more reliable conclusions about the effectiveness of LLM-guided discovery.

title: Fragment-Based Virtual Screening and Experimental Validation of MMP-9 Hemopexinlike Domain Inhibitors
tldr: This paper presents an integrated fragment-based drug discovery (FBDD) approach that combines pharmacophore modeling, structure-based virtual screening, molecular dynamics simulations, and extensive biological validation to identify novel MMP-9 PEX domain inhibitors. The study focuses on matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9), a key mediator of extracellular matrix remodeling and cancer metastasis, for which the development of selective inhibitors has been challenging due to high conservation of its catalytic domain. The work highlights the discovery of potential novel MMP-9 PEX domain inhibitors, offering a promising chemical scaffold for further preclinical development, although the specific efficacy and selectivity of these compounds remain to be determined in more detailed studies.

title: Gromov-Monge Flow Matching for Equivariant Graph Generation
tldr: This paper introduces Gromov-Monge Flow Matching for generating equivariant graphs, improving sample quality in continuous and categorical data generation at small integration budgets. Notably, this approach excels in flow matching, where symmetry in source-target coupling is considered within the graph quotient space, leading to improved model performance compared to conventional many-step sampling.

title: Temperature-induced Changes to the Nucleation Mechanism of MOF-5-inspired Crystals through the Lens of Multiscale Simulation
tldr: This study employs molecular simulation to investigate the impact of temperature on the nucleation mechanism of MOF-5-inspired crystals. A multiscale approach, including coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations enhanced with Hamiltonian replica exchange, is used to construct free energy surfaces and minimum free energy pathway analysis. The results suggest that the temperature of 413 K, as typically used in MOF-5's solvothermal synthesis in DMF, is more kinetically favorable compared to both 300 K and 500 K, offering valuable insights for optimizing crystal growth processes.

title: Development of the 12-6-4-3B Model: Incorporating Nonadditive Three-Body Interactions into Metal Ion Simulations
tldr: The 12-6-4-3B model, a refined classical force field, is proposed based on Extended Discrete Averaging Potentials (EDA) and physical reasoning. This model introduces three-body interactions, significantly improving its accuracy in simulating [Zn(H2O)n]2+ clusters (n = 2 - 6), particularly in reproducing the water exchange mechanism and associated free energy barrier. This enhancement underscores the practical benefit of considering nonadditive three-body effects in metal ion simulations.
